column1: # p374 — THE REGIONAL-LEG REGISTER.  ACTION p373-A, limb 1.  THE OWNED HOME Gap 489 ASKED FOR.
# 🟢 Gap 489: "This base has published FOUR different attributions for what makes a regional leg
# work -- ACTION PJ (organ), ACTION QJ (shape was never the defect), P870 (jurisdiction phrasing),
# Gap 476 (language) -- in FOUR different files, none citing another.  There is no single place
# where 'what makes a regional leg work' is recorded."  🟢 THIS FILE IS THAT PLACE.  Every later
# claim about regional legs cites this register or amends it; no fifth file.
# 🔴 TWO CORRECTIONS TO ACTION p373-A AS IT WAS WRITTEN, both measured before building the column.
# 🔴 (1) THE DENOMINATOR.  p373-A says "the column is derivable for the 8 jurisdictions already
# carried".  Counted first-hand over the nine SHELF_FILES this pass commits, the base names at
# least 21: Brazil 244, India 224, China 173, Korea 147, Chile 137, Singapore 112, Mexico 111,
# Colombia 91, Japan 88, Canada 79, Germany 76, France 55, Peru 54, Spain 51, Australia 50,
# Netherlands 42, Argentina 41, Uruguay 32, Italy 15, Portugal 14, Quebec 5 (word-boundary
# matches).  "8" was an estimate published as a denominator.  The register carries all 21 and
# marks the 15 that are UNMEASURED as unmeasured, because a blank cell is information and an
# absent row is not.
# 🔴 (2) THE COLUMN p373-A SPECIFIED IS THE WRONG COLUMN, and building it as specified would have
# wired a refuted theory into a standing gate.  p373-A asks for "a per-jurisdiction CORPUS-LANGUAGE
# column so a leg's adequacy is checkable".  That column presupposes p373's account -- that what
# decides a leg is the language THE JURISDICTION publishes in.  🔴 p374's cell O5 refutes it on a
# pre-registered prediction: Japan publishes its guidelines in Japanese and the ENGLISH leg was
# productive anyway, through MLex and English news wires.  🟢 The column that actually predicts the
# six measured cells is the one below: DOES A CROSS-BORDER SPECIALIST PRESS CHANNEL COVER THIS
# JURISDICTION'S EDUCATION POLICY IN THE QUERY LANGUAGE, AND WHICH ONE.
# COLUMNS.  measured_by: the pass that ran the leg first-hand -- never an inference from prose.
# en_leg / inlang_leg: PRODUCTIVE | PARTIAL | NIL | UNMEASURED.
# en_channel: the named outlet that carried the facts on the English leg, or NONE-FOUND.
# fact_class_differs: did the in-language leg return a DIFFERENT class of fact, not merely more?

column1: # 🔴 THE FIGURE THIS REGISTER EXISTS TO MAKE VISIBLE: 21 jurisdictions carried, 7 ever reached by
# a first-hand regional leg, 14 never.  Two of the 7 (Mexico, Quebec) rest on a single draw from
# p207, 167 passes ago.  🟢 The base's regional claims are therefore built on 5 live cells, and
# until this file existed that was not visible anywhere.
# 🟢 THE STANDING RULE THIS REGISTER CARRIES, replacing the one-limb I4 (see p374-regional-leg):
#   A published regional NIL is admissible only if (limb 1) the leg NAMED a jurisdiction -- a
#   country or an organ, not a region label like "EMEA" -- AND (limb 2) an in-language leg was
#   also run for that same jurisdiction.  🔴 p373's cell 1 is exactly what limb 1 exists to
#   refuse: an in-language leg naming no jurisdiction, which returned an explicit nil for every
#   EMEA country except the language's own.  I4 would have passed it.
#   AND: no pass may call a language REDUNDANT for a jurisdiction unless both legs ran AND
#   returned the SAME fact class.  🔴 Japan is the negative control: both legs productive, and
#   the Japanese leg returned the only operational figure either leg produced.
